taxonomy.note: Older field guides and nursery sources may still use the former genus Gaura; preserve those names as synonyms but use current Oenothera placement canonically.

evidence: Hays — project Hays-local source pool contains 6 wild/noncultivated observations and flags the species as Hays Local; this is supporting occurrence evidence rather than a herbarium voucher.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index includes Gaura suffulta var. suffulta, the former genus treatment of Oenothera suffulta.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed treatment under the accepted name Oenothera suffulta.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county occurrence inferred from statewide native status; named counties are supported by explicit local/herbarium/project occurrence evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Compare the flower and fruit together: this annual has a mostly glabrous flowering spike with white 12–19 mm four-petaled flowers, crimson anthers, and a short chunky nutlike fruit with four major lobes/ridges.
diagnostic_traits: vegetative stems/leaves villous but flowering spike essentially glabrous
radial white flowers about 12–19 mm across
short indehiscent 4-sided/4-lobed nutlike fruit about 6–7 mm

confusers.separator: O. suffulta has much larger flowers (12–19 mm versus ~3 mm), a cleaner essentially glabrous inflorescence, and chunky 4-lobed fruit; O. curtiflora is densely velveteen with minute flowers and narrow fruit.
O. suffulta is annual and has radial white flowers and a chunky nutlike fruit; O. lindheimeri is a tall perennial clump with airy one-sided flowers and long projecting stamens.
